title: CISA Adds Three Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
summary:
CISA has added three new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

  • CVE-2026-120705 OSGeo GeoServer XML Injection Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-129243 OSGeo GeoServer Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-136716 Drupal Core Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions Vulnerability 

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

summary:

$ ansible-playbook main.yml -K

PLAY [Security] *******************************************************

TASK [Gathering Facts] ***********************************************************************

title: UniFi Network Application 11.1.58
summary:
Overview

UniFi Network Application 11.1.58 includes the improvements and bugfixes listed below.

Improvements

  • Added a Firmware Revert option for U5G devices.

  • Added support for local Firewall Policies when using Orchestration Engine Firewall Policies.

  • Added a Refresh Interval option to Historical Flows.

  • Added device progress indicators to Topology.

  • Added System Log events for public WAN IP address changes.

  • Added alarms for 5G SIM changes, client roaming, and AP channel changes.

  • Added Threat Signature filtering to Traffic Flows.

  • Added usage statistics to Object-Oriented Networking objects.

  • Added support for larger Live Flows counts.

    • Requires UniFi OS Gateway 6.1 or newer.

  • Added System Logs for Matter devices.

  • Added support for saving IGMP Querier addresses on non-querier switches.

  • Added Port Automations to automatically apply Port Profiles based on the connected device's vendor or MAC OUI.

  • Added a Wake-on-LAN option for wired clients.

    • Wake-on-LAN must be supported and enabled in the device's settings, such as its power settings or BIOS/UEFI. The device must remain connected to power, with its network adapter powered while asleep or shut down.

  • Improved Internet settings.

    • Added support for multiple VLANs on the same port.

    • Added a Passthrough VLANs setting.

  • Improved the Hotspot user experience.

    • Added a Personal Password for Each Guest option to generate unique passwords for guests to use across their devices.

    • Added an Isolate Guests option to assign each Personal WiFi guest to a separate network.

    • Added Guest Details to the Clients and Guests side panels.

    • Added an option to collect guest email addresses and export them via CSV or send them through Webhooks.

    • Added Webhook notifications when guest access ends.

    • Added CSV export and custom date selection.

    • Added support for custom fields, such as Student ID, in External Authorization.

    • Added support for Walled Garden links in Hotspot Landing Page settings.

    • Added an option to remove Powered by UniFi from the Hotspot Landing Page.

    • Improved External Authorization integration.

    • Improved guest data limit enforcement accuracy.

    • Improved guest authorization handling so revoking access for offline guests takes effect immediately on access points and gateways.

  • Improved the Orchestration Engine.

    • Added Device Template support.

    • Added Hotspot support.

    • Added Supernets support, allowing automatic subnet generation to prevent overlaps across sites.

    • Added Static Route support.

    • Added Port Profiles and Port Automations support.

  • Improved DHCP Guarding by synchronizing the configured IP address with the gateway IP for existing automatically created networks.

  • Improved Object creation by previewing automatically generated objects before saving.

  • Improved Channel AI.

  • Improved SD-WAN stability by preventing unnecessary tunnel reconnections on failover hubs when adding spokes.

  • Improved mesh adoption to prevent changes to Mesh Parent settings on other access points.

  • Improved statistics engine resiliency.

  • Improved application stability.

Bugfixes

  • Fixed an issue where the Site Manager Internet Health bar could temporarily show a site as offline after a Network Application update.

  • Fixed incorrect device time reporting for the Manitoba and Yukon time zones.

  • Fixed an issue where switch settings could not be edited after enabling Layer 3 routing.

  • Fixed an issue where devices connected to QSFP28 ports could display incorrect port numbers.

  • Fixed an issue where the Kill Switch could block internet access when a routed VPN client was paused.

  • Fixed an issue where Shadow Mode standby consoles could lose their Shadow Mode configuration if power was interrupted during a restore.

  • Fixed an issue where MC-LAG peer-link port configuration could drop keepalive traffic or tagged VLANs.

  • Fixed an issue where Port Lock did not work correctly with the main and backup ports of E7 access points.

  • Fixed an issue where blocking a client could fail when a nearby unadopted device was running older firmware.

  • Fixed an issue where blocked traffic from WireGuard clients was not displayed in Traffic Flows.

  • Fixed an issue where the UniFi Cellular Internet Backup option could be missing from Network settings.

  • Fixed a rare issue where Integration API requests could stall for up to 40 seconds.

  • Fixed an issue where UPS 2U Pro outlets could not be powered off remotely.

  • Fixed an issue where Site Manager could display incorrect Internet Health information.

  • Fixed an issue where some UniFi devices could show incorrect hostnames.

Additional information

 

Self-Hosted UniFi Deployments

For self-hosted deployments, we recommend transitioning to UniFi OS Server, which provides the full UniFi OS Platform experience, including the latest features, improvements, and integrations.

UniFi Cloud Gateways remain our recommended solution for deployments that do not require self-hosting.

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-127280
C-More EA9 Programming Software V6.80 does not adequately validate data read from a project file before using it in heap memory operations. A crafted file causes a heap buffer overrun during file open, resulting in heap corruption and instability within the application. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by convincing a user to open a malicious project file delivered through common distribution channels such as email, file sharing, or removable media.

Remediations

Vendor fix

Mitigation
If you cannot update to the latest software or firmware version right away, apply the following compensating controls to reduce risk until the update can be performed. These measures are temporary and do not replace the update, which remains the primary and recommended remediation. Apply these controls as appropriate based on the vulnerability, assessed risk, operational requirements, and characteristics of your environment. Implement changes under your established management-of-change process. Before implementing isolation, access-control, or network-configuration changes, evaluate potential impacts to safety, availability, and essential operational functions. • Isolate affected engineering workstations and OT systems from external and nonessential networks, including the internet and corporate IT networks, where operationally feasible. • Disable or tightly restrict vendor, contractor, and other remote access to the affected OT environment until the vulnerability can be remediated. Where remote access is operationally required, use a hardened jump host, enforce multi-factor authentication, apply least-privilege access, and limit access to authorized, time-bound sessions. • Use trusted, dedicated OT networks for device communication. Where practicable and appropriate to the assessed risk, use dedicated or physically separated infrastructure for higher-criticality systems. Where logical segmentation is used, ensure segmentation controls are appropriately configured, secured, and monitored. • Restrict both physical and logical access to affected systems to authorized personnel only. Apply least-privilege principles to administrative, engineering, maintenance, and service access. • Configure application allowlisting, where supported, so that only trusted and pre-approved applications are permitted to execute. Block unauthorized software. • Use appropriate antivirus or endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools where supported and compatible with the affected system. Configure host-based and network firewalls to permit only required communications. • Disable unnecessary services, ports, protocols, and communication pathways associated with the affected systems. Where a service or protocol cannot be disabled for operational reasons, restrict access to trusted systems and authorized users wherever possible. • Enable and regularly review available system, security, and network logs to identify suspicious or unauthorized activity. Where appropriate, monitor communications to and from affected systems for unexpected connections or changes in network behavior. • Maintain secure, tested, and preferably offline backups of PLC programs, device configurations, engineering workstation configurations, and other information necessary to restore operations. Periodically verify that backups can be successfully restored. • Verify that critical OT functions can continue operating without unnecessary dependencies on external networks, cloud services, remote-access services, corporate IT services, or other nonessential systems. • If removable media is required to transfer files into an isolated or restricted environment, use controlled and trusted media and scan it for malicious content before use. • Continuously evaluate the risks associated with operating vulnerable or outdated firmware or software. Adjust compensating controls as the threat environment, operational requirements, or available vulnerability information changes. These compensating controls are intended to reduce exposure while remediation is pending. Organizations should prioritize applying the vendor-provided update as soon as it can be safely tested and deployed within the operational environment.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

CISA also recommends users take the following measures to protect themselves from social engineering attacks:

  • Do not click web links or open attachments in unsolicited email messages.
  • Refer to Recognizing and Avoiding Email Scams for more information on avoiding email scams.
  • Refer to Avoiding Social Engineering and Phishing Attacks for more information on social engineering attacks.

No known public exploitation specifically targeting these vulnerabilities has been reported to CISA at this time.

  • CVE-2024-10441 Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-40217 BerriAI LiteLLM Unprotected Alternate Channel Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-90436 Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-90817 Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. 

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. 

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. 

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
summary: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.

title: Noctua Fan Swap on a Calnex Rb/GPS Frequency Reference
summary:
Since this will be the only source of this process on the Internet1, I figured I'd document a quick fan swap I did on a piece of test/reference equipment I'm running in my Atomic Clock Tower.

I took my Torx T10 screwdriver and popped off the top cover. The screws required some force to loosen, as they were all secured with Loctite.

The inside is simple and serviceable. There's a SpectraTime GRClok-1500, with an integrated timing-grade GPS module, and a stabilized 10 MHz output2.

title: UniFi Network Application 11.0.97
summary:
Overview

UniFi Network Application 11.0.97 requires UniFi OS 6.0 or newer. The upgrade may take up to 20 minutes.

 

Improved Application Stability

  • Migrated the application database to PostgreSQL.

  • Introduced a new, more scalable statistics engine.

  • Existing statistics history is cleared and starts fresh after the update.

  • Removed USG gateway support.

  • Network Application 10.6 is the last version supporting USG.

  • Removed Network Application Server support.

  • Upgrade to UniFi OS Server, the official replacement.

  • All sites are automatically migrated to the Zone-Based Firewall.

Live Flows

View active flows on the gateway while they are in progress and terminate them on demand.

  • Supported on UDM-Pro, UDM-SE, UDM-Pro-Max, UDW, EFG, EF-Core, UDM-Beast, UCG-Fiber, UCG-Max, UXG-Max, UXG-Fiber, UXG-Pro, and UXG-Enterprise.

  • Requires UniFi OS 6.0.10 or newer.

  • UniFi Gateways (UXG) require a UCK-Enterprise, Official Hosting, or UniFi OS Server.

External Network Lists

Added an External source option to Network Lists to import domain or IP lists from external sources.

  • Requires UniFi OS 6.0.10 or newer.

WiFi Uplink

Connect your gateway to a nearby WiFi network to use as an internet backup.

  • Supported on UDR-7, UDR-5G-Max, Express 7, and UCG-Industrial.

  • Requires UniFi OS 6.0.10 or newer.

Matter Thread Device Monitoring

Commission Matter Thread devices to monitor their status and connectivity.

  • Requires a Cloud Gateway with UniFi OS 6.0.10 or newer.

  • mDNS must be enabled.

  • IPv6 must be enabled on the network hosting the Thread Border Routers.

Improvements

  • Added an option to generate client device icons.

  • Added a new client connection alarm.

  • Added Battery Self-Test for UPS devices.

  • Added bulk editing for clients, including removal and blocking.

  • Added a country selection dropdown to Channel Plan.

  • Added support for Subnet Overlap System Logs.

  • Added Time Machine to the Topology page.

  • Added IPIP WAN support for Japanese IPv4 over IPv6 services.

  • Added a Packet Capture option to the Radio side panel.

  • Added Remote Power Cycle support for UPS 2U Pro.

  • Added a USB-C option for EAV-Bridge.

  • Added date selection for Port Manager statistics.

  • Added SD-WAN Policies for destination- and performance-based routing across selected spokes, with configurable hub selection, WAN priorities, and tunnel health thresholds for packet loss, latency, and jitter.

    • Requires Site Manager 5.10.2 or newer.

  • Improved traffic animations in Topology.

  • Improved guest authorization latency through the API.

  • Improved switch stacking stability.

  • Improved the 802.1X and RADIUS settings user experience.

  • Improved Channel AI.

  • Improved IGMP Snooping settings validation.

  • Improved the firmware Revert experience with a feedback form.

  • Improved the Deep Inspection settings user experience.

  • Improved Port Manager default columns and filters.

  • Improved Time Machine loading performance on large sites.

  • Improved the VPN settings user experience.

  • Improved availability detection for Virtual Network Override.

  • Improved the Routing settings user experience.

  • Increased the VLAN limit when no gateway is adopted.

  • Time Machine now remembers whether it was open or closed.

  • Updated Site-to-Site OpenVPN encryption options with AES-192-CBC and AES-128-CBC support.

  • Revoked compromised eMudhra CA certificates.

  • Removed System Settings when using Site Manager.

    • Language and Time settings are now managed through the Site Manager header and synchronized across UniFi applications.

    • Country selection is now available in WiFi Channel settings.

    • NTP settings are now available in the Site Gateway side panel.

    • The Professional Installer section has been removed, with Extend 6 GHz Non-PSC Channel Use now available in Global WiFi settings.

    • System Settings remain available in the Local Portal for Language and Time configuration.

Flows

  • Added Firewall Policy names for Allow actions in Traffic Flows.

  • Added support for reordering columns in Traffic Flows.

    • Requires UniFi OS 6.0.10 or newer.

  • Added Application Column/Filter in Traffic Flows.

    • Requires UniFi OS 6.0.10 or newer.

  • Added a Flows Logging option to Firewall Policies.

  • Improved Traffic Flows reporting.

  • Local DNS queries are now identified as DNS in Traffic Flows.

Bugfixes

  • Fixed an issue where Channel AI could suggest channels unavailable to outdoor access points.

  • Fixed an issue where disabling the display on a meshed Express 7 could fail.

  • Fixed a rare issue where Alarm Manager emails could be sent unexpectedly.

  • Fixed an issue where Firewall Policies referencing SD-WAN hub-spoke tunnels could stop working after WAN interface changes.

  • Fixed missing System Log events for unauthorized Hotspot guests.

  • Fixed a rare issue where hostname and IPv6 address information could fluctuate.

  • Fixed an issue where an incorrect parent device could be offered when adopting a UniFi Device Bridge.

  • Fixed a rare issue where leaving a web session open for an extended period could cause the browser to crash.

  • Fixed an issue where L2TP VPN appeared as a Content Filtering source option.

  • Fixed a rare issue where devices could appear twice in the Devices list.

  • Fixed a rare issue where guest voucher authorization could report success without providing internet access.

  • Fixed a rare issue where Hotspot guests could be required to reauthorize when roaming between access points.

  • Fixed a rare issue where SD-WAN tunnels could fail to establish between sites.

  • Fixed an issue where Isolated Networks did not isolate traffic to the VPN zone.

  • Fixed a rare issue where IPv6 IPS threats did not appear in Traffic Flows.

  • Fixed an issue where Site Manager could fail to display statistics for multi-site hosts with a large number of sites.

Additional information

title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

title: Upgrade your PHP installs immediately to protect against php2shell
summary:
This morning, two critical PHP Security Advisories were published:

  • RCE via OOM corruption (9.2/10)
  • RCE via stale global state (9.2/10)

If you're running PHP for any service, you need to upgrade immediately to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, or 8.5.12. And if you use Remi's repos on RedHat-derivative Linux distros, you need to switch to official repos temporarily as Remi's on vacation and can't update his community repo. (Reminds me of xkcd 2347). Remi pushed updates even while on vacation!

title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
summary: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

title: Formlabs dropped the Raspberry Pi on the way to a $699 SLA printer
summary:
Formlabs sent me a Form Studio 1 resin 3D printer to test after years of back-and-forth about their Form 4 printer.

Like the Form 4, it's an SLA (stereolithography) printer, but unlike the Form 4 (which starts at $2,600), it's affordable for a hobbyist. It's not cheap, coming in at $699 (or $749 with a flex build platform, which I highly recommend), but it is affordable.

I can't say as much about this printer as people who are well-versed in resin printing and use other SLA printers (all my experience until now is with FDM, or Fused Deposition Modeling1, printers). But I can convey my first-time experience using this printer and with the entire SLA experience.

title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
summary: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.
